derivation: STATIC ONLY. Every number below was computed offline by reading the committed package-lock.json out of the reconciled archive. No install was run, so nothing here is an observed installed tree — it is what the lockfile says would be installed.

lockState.honestNote: The lockfile's root name and version agree with package.json, so this candidate carries none of the lockfile-to-manifest drift seen in the factoriolab lane.

closure.closureIsFullyPinned: every entry carries an exact version; 1524 of 1722 additionally carry a registry URL and an integrity hash

integrityGapExplained.whatTheyAre: All 198 are `bundled: true, optional: true` entries nested inside fsevents@1.x, which appears three times in the tree (under @angular/compiler-cli, watchpack, and webpack-dev-server — 66 entries each).
integrityGapExplained.whyNoIntegrity: npm 6 records bundled dependencies by name and version only, because they ship inside the parent package's own tarball and are covered by that tarball's integrity hash rather than by their own. This is normal lockfileVersion 1 behaviour, not a gap in the pinning.
integrityGapExplained.platformNote: fsevents is a darwin-only optional dependency. On a non-darwin host these 198 entries are skipped entirely.

closure.devSkewNote: The dev/production split is read from the lockfile's own `dev` flags. It is lopsided because the whole Angular 8 build toolchain (CLI, devkit, webpack 4, karma, protractor, puppeteer, tslint, codelyzer) is declared as devDependencies while the shipped application depends on a much smaller runtime set.

frameworkAndToolchain.compiler: View Engine — Angular 8 predates Ivy-by-default and tsconfig.app.json sets no enableIvy flag; the production configuration builds AOT
frameworkAndToolchain.nativeBridge: @ionic-native/{core,in-app-browser,splash-screen,status-bar} 5.0.0-beta.15 — pinned to a beta, recorded as found
frameworkAndToolchain.stateLibrary: none — no NgRx, no Redux; state lives in two injectable providers (user-data, conference-data) over @ionic/storage

serviceWorker.registration: src/app/app.module.ts calls ServiceWorkerModule.register('ngsw-worker.js', ...) — the service worker REGISTERS
serviceWorker.buildFlag: angular.json sets serviceWorker:true on the production configuration only, so a --prod build emits ngsw-worker.js and ngsw.json while a development build does not
serviceWorker.witnessTimeNote: Recorded here as presence, per the packet. The HospitalRun non-masking precedent governs how a registering service worker is handled at witness time; nothing about that is decided by this record.
serviceWorker.pwaPackagePlacementOddity: @angular/pwa is a schematics package and normally lives in devDependencies; here it is declared in dependencies. Recorded as found.

cordova.platformPackages: cordova-android ^8.1.0, cordova-ios ^5.1.1 — declared as runtime dependencies
cordova.relevance: The browser build target does not depend on these. They are recorded because they are part of the honest dependency shape and they inflate the install.

lifecycleScripts.preRuledHandling: npm ci --ignore-scripts, recorded as a labeled deviation (PM, 2026-08-10)
lifecycleScripts.buildDependenceOnPostinstall: NOT ESTABLISHED. No install and no build were run by this unit. The static reading is that webdriver-manager only populates Selenium and Chromedriver binaries consumed by the protractor e2e target, which @angular-devkit/build-angular:browser does not reference — but that is an inference from the manifest, not an observed outcome, and the unknown is preserved.

backend.evidence: The tree contains no server source, no Dockerfile and no docker-compose file. The application reads its conference dataset from src/assets/data/data.json, copied into dist as an asset, and persists user state (login, favourites, tutorial-seen) through @ionic/storage in the browser. firebase.json and .firebaserc are present and configure static hosting for the built output, not an application backend.
backend.networkAtRuntime: a static asset fetch of assets/data/data.json from the app's own origin, plus — on the map tab only — a runtime script injection against the Google Maps JavaScript API, which the packet excludes and which must be inventoried as a blocked request at witness time

nonclaims: These figures are read from a committed lockfile, not from an installed tree. They establish what the lockfile pins. They establish nothing about whether those versions are still fetchable, whether they install, whether they build, or what they are licensed under.
No licence determination is made for any dependency in this closure.
